title: A Lot of Stocks Have Crashed: How to Spot Opportunities vs Traps | Rahul Jain
creator: Rahul Jain
summary: Rahul Jain teaches a Tickertape screening method for finding beaten-down stocks that may rebound, starting from Nifty near 22,700 after a fall from about 26,000, with small caps down 40-70%. He restricts his universe to stocks above ₹28,000 crore market cap (roughly the top 300), arguing small caps carry high valuation risk, then filters for stocks at least 20% away from their 52-week high and 0-10% away from their 52-week low, so upside to the old high exceeds downside to the old low; that leaves 96 names. He adds PE and PB premium versus sub-sector and a custom forward PEG (forward PE divided by one-year forward EPS growth), keeping PEG between 0 and 1.5, which leaves 32 names. He stresses the list changes daily; none are recommendations. As worked examples only, he reviews Bajaj Finserv - revenue growth moderating, insurance weak on motor growth and underwriting margins but lending strong, Q1 total income up about 19% and PAT up about 18%, with a stated aim of about 20% revenue CAGR to 2030 and PAT 2.5 times - and calls it worth reviewing in more detail. On Tata Steel he stops early: West Asia disruption and about ₹1,200 crore of unplanned cost in the quarter are continuing risks. On Canara Bank he would wait for Q2 results: special mention accounts have risen from MSME and retail, an early NPA warning, even though advances grew about 18%. He warns the strategy is risky and fallen stocks can fall further. Captions are clean.
